title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Deployment Allowance by Extensions Recorded on a Military Service Hold
content:
**Schedule.** When current proof of active military duty is asked for before a status review of a running Military Service Hold under Hardship and Protective Holds, the extension-history allowance of the status review proof depends on the extensions recorded on the hold (the extension grants in its history). Repeatedly extended orders usually mean a deployment that slows any proof. The allowance is added once to the days allowed for the status review proof.

| Extensions recorded on the hold | Extension-history allowance |
|---|---|
| At least the repeat-extension count of 2 | 10 calendar days (repeat-extension days) |
| Exactly 1 | 5 calendar days (single-extension days) |
| None | Nothing |

**Both sides.** One recorded extension: 5 days. Two: 10 days. Three: 10 days. None: nothing.

**Example (hypothetical).** A hold whose history shows extensions numbered 1 and 2: two extensions recorded, so 10 calendar days are added.
